title: CLaRE-ty Amid Chaos: Quantifying Representational Entanglement to Predict Ripple Effects in LLM Editing
abstract: arXiv:2603.19297v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The static knowledge representations of large language models (LLMs) inevitably become outdated or incorrect over time. While model-editing techniques offer a promising solution by modifying a model's factual associations, they often produce unpredictable ripple effects, which are unintended behavioral changes that propagate even to the hidden space. In this work, we introduce CLaRE, a lightweight representation-level technique to identify where these ripple effects may occur. Unlike prior gradient-based methods, CLaRE quantifies entanglement between facts using forward activations from a single intermediate layer, avoiding costly backward passes. To enable systematic study, we prepare and analyse a corpus of 11,427 facts drawn from three existing datasets. translated_title: 混乱中的“CLaRE-ty”（清晰度）：量化表征纠缠以预测大语言模型编辑中的涟漪效应
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）的静态知识表征随着时间推移不可避免地会变得过时或错误。虽然模型编辑技术通过修改模型的事实关联提供了一种有前景的解决方案，但它们常常产生不可预测的涟漪效应，即甚至能传播到隐藏空间的非预期行为变化。在这项工作中，我们提出了CLaRE，这是一种轻量级的表征层面的技术，用于识别这些涟漪效应可能发生的位置。与以往基于梯度的方法不同，CLaRE使用来自单个中间层的前向激活来量化事实之间的纠缠程度，从而避免了代价高昂的反向传播。为了实现系统性研究，我们准备并分析了从三个现有数据集中提取的11,427条事实组成的语料库。利用CLaRE，我们为多个模型计算了该语料库的大规模纠缠图，以捕捉局部编辑如何在表征空间中传播。这些图使我们能够……
tldr: 本文提出CLaRE，一种轻量级的表征层面技术，仅利用单个中间层的前向激活（无需昂贵的反向传播）量化事实之间的纠缠程度，从而预测大语言模型编辑中涟漪效应可能发生的位置。
en_tdlr: CLaRE is a lightweight representation-level technique that quantifies entanglement between facts using forward activations from a single intermediate layer—avoiding costly backward passes—to predict where ripple effects may occur in LLM editing.
